item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 9
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched The Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 9 twice. In this episode, the poison was alcohol and salt, and sweetness was involved too.

Gaoshun was like a father to Jinshi. He also said he had known Jinshi since he was a kid, and he was surprised by Jinshi's childish behavior toward Maomao. He didn't seem to welcome it because Jinshi should behave like a higher-up, so he is a strict and disciplined person.

When I saw Maomao drinking alcohol, I wondered how old she was. But it made sense that there was no age restriction on drinking it at that time. She was also upset and acted her age, which was rare. Jinshi was trying to pass a bill forbidding teenagers from drinking alcohol. He was so happy when he found her weakness.

When her dad said she might make medicine out of a corpse and she might dig up graves, it totally made sense that she shouldn't cross that line. He really understood her well and he gave her good advice. Jinshi and Gaoshun were also able to imagine she would do it, so they understood who she was.

When they were trying to figure out why a maid had died near the wall, it was a little out of the blue to me why Maomao started thinking about how she wanted to die. She even asked Jinshi to have her killed in the way she preferred. The sequence where she imagined how she wanted to die was drawn in red, as red suggests blood and can be seen as deadly. And in that scene, she was thinking about people who had nearly died, or who were trying to kill someone. There were so many attempts to assassinate someone up to this point, surprisingly.

In the last scene, why did Jinshi look for someone who had their arms burned? Was it related to someone who poisoned somebody at the garden party? I forgot, but by the end of this episode it turns out to be related to Consort Ah-Duo and her head lady-in-waiting.

Scores

  • Episode: 5/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • She showed she was afraid of being forbidden to drink alcohol. It seemed to be rare and she looked like a kid
  • Maomao's Dad: 7/10
    • The advice he gave Maomao was so good.
  • Jinshi: 7/10
    • He showed his childish behavior when he was given the runaround.
    • He also tried to solve a rear palace issue like an adult
  • Gaoshun: 7/10
    • Gaoshun was like a father to Jinshi, probably strict and disciplined. Maybe a good father
  • Quack doctor: 6/10
    • He worked in the rear palace, and unlike Maomao, who had already seen a few deadly scenes, he still wasn't used to seeing an autopsy. Not courageous, and easily frightened

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 8
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 8 twice.

Well, this episode was probably just a side story in the Verdigris House. Maomao's dad was really good, but it was hard to confirm he was right. She might have imagined he was that good and that he was able to guess it from only a small amount of evidence, though he didn't say a word. And also, why didn't he say anything other than asking her a couple of questions? So, I couldn't figure out whether he was really that talented or not. Also, from the result of Maomao's conjecture, it would have been almost magic if he had deduced it. There were 2 drinks and I couldn't figure it out until she worked it through. That said, he didn't receive the money, which included a hush-money fee. So he might have known that at least that person was suspicious. So, they all planned to poison him.

In terms of Jinshi, he got so upset that it was great to watch, and he showed some emotions he had never shown on his face. So, by episode 8, he had already fallen in love with Maomao, obviously, not just interested in her. And obviously, she was probably the only one he couldn't charm at all, because everyone else was attracted to Jinshi for his high rank and how cool he was. Maomao was so dense, or just avoided thinking about it unconsciously, so it would take more time for him to date her. Gyokuyou found it so funny and laughed a lot when she overheard the exchange between him and Maomao. Assuming he was the Emperor's brother, for Gyokuyou, he was like a brother-in-law, though she wasn't the Empress. So, she might have felt he was like a child, and she was happy to see Jinshi act his age.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • She respected and tried to learn things from her dad, and was honest with him
    • She didn't give a hoot about Jinshi at all
    • I was impressed with Aoi Yuki's voice actingg to talk in a low pitch when she treated the two people
  • Maomao's Dad: 5/10
    • He was so quiet and didn't put much into words for Maomao
  • Jinshi: 8/10
    • His shock at what Maomao said was a good one
  • Lady Gyokuyou: 8/10
    • She enjoyed the funny exchange between Jinshi and Maomao like a friend hearing a funny story
  • Lihaku: 5/10
    • A normal person who was attracted to a courtesan

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 7
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 7 twice.

The episode started the day after the garden party in the previous episode. I wondered where Maomao was sleeping in such a good bed, but it was one of the rooms in the Jade Pavilion.

It was rare that Maomao and Gaoshun talked about issues without Jinshi, so it felt odd to me. But Jinshi seemed to be wiped out, so Gaoshun needed to do it by himself. Also, it was originally her own request, so it made sense. Maomao thought Lady Lishu couldn't read the room at first, but she figured out it was because she was bullied. So, it was great that that first impression actually had a reason behind it. Jinshi also showed his lazy, easygoing side to Gaoshun. Yeah, that was a young man who acts sociable for other people. When Gyokuyou teased him, he was so upset and she found it so funny. It was nice to see her like that.

Lihaku was also a character who gave a hairpin to every girl but didn't take it seriously. Well, but he wasn't really a kind guy and he did that for... why? I don't know. Anyhow, that was good for Maomao, because she didn't care about him at all. She also negotiated well because she showed the hairpins she had received from other people, as if she had more options. In fact, the other two wouldn't have been interested in the same invitation. But he was a man, so he couldn't turn down an invitation to the Verdigris House. I also wondered whether her gift was too generous just to get herself home, but it turned out the madam had thought it through and wanted to attract more loyal customers.

Maomao's adoptive father wasn't surprised at all when he saw her. I guess the madam of the Verdigris House let him know what had happened to Maomao, because Maomao had been sending letters to her, not to him. So, he didn't look all that pleased, but he was quietly happy and listened to her.

I wonder how much of Maomao's conjecture is actually true. I don't remember what actually happened, so it's going to be fun to watch it.

Scores

  • Episode: 7/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • She took care of Lady Lishu's food taster regardless of what she did, because their lives were "expendable". She was kind and forgiving to many people
    • She can lift fingerprints like a detective, and she can negotiate like a sales representative.
  • Jinshi: 8/10
    • Showed a different side of him — lazy and easygoing
  • Gaoshun: 7/10
    • How old was he? He knew Jinshi from the start, so he must be old.
    • He was so mature and got along with Jinshi and Maomao well
  • Lady Gyokuyou: 8/10
    • She had a playful side, so she teased Jinshi and enjoyed it
  • Lihaku: 6/10
    • He gave out hairpins for some reason, but it was only superficial
    • He also didn't want to give Maomao the time of day, so he wasn't kind or nice

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 6
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 6 twice. From this episode, things got complicated and interesting.

I wondered in the previous episode why Lady Lishu wore a different color from her ladies-in-waiting — dark pink, while they wore white. But Maomao mentioned it, though there was no answer for that, so we may be able to figure it out later.

I wonder how many hairpins each person has. Lihaku had many of them, so there was no limit, but I don't think someone like Lihua gave them to many random people. And also, why did Lihaku want to give them to that many people? I forgot.

It was odd that Consort Lishu had been a consort of the previous Emperor — the current Emperor's stepmother, in effect — when she was younger. I mean, why did the previous Emperor marry a nine-year-old girl? It sounded like there was a war between Lishu's original country and that country, and she was married to the previous Emperor to make peace between those countries. Will we know the details later?

In terms of food tasting, this episode really showed how Maomao was off her rocker when it came to poisons. She knew she needed to lie down and felt like a dog after taking poison, but she still loved it and wanted to swallow it. I guess it was like alcohol for her. The other food taster was really scared of eating the food, and it made sense as it's hard to tell whether a dish contains poison. And if they eat a lot, they may kick the bucket. Maomao also thought a food taster was expendable. This scene was great as many series do not care how these high-ranking people avoided poisons, and in this series, we can feel it.

Well, in terms of Lady Lishu and her ladies-in-waiting, was it intentional, and did Lady Lishu have to eat the mackerel? The lady-in-waiting's face obviously showed she knew it, so she was scared when Maomao intimidated her. If your food taster doesn't stop you from eating the poison, and you're in a situation where you're forced to eat, that's a terrible situation. Why didn't people stop this custom, honestly? I guess a few of them died at these garden parties in the past.

There was no brother of the Emperor at the party, but considering Gaoshun was high-ranking and he followed Jinshi, it was obvious that Jinshi was the Emperor's brother. I didn't remember exactly, but I thought he was the son of the Emperor, the next Emperor. Maomao somehow didn't think deeply when it came to him. Maybe she didn't care about him at all.

Scores

  • Score: 8/10
  • Maomao: 9/10
    • Aoi Yuki's voice acting was so good in the details. I was able to feel different small emotions from different behaviors.
    • This was mainly an episode about her as a food taster, and it showed how talented and crazy she was
    • Also she helped Lady Lishu, and she was nice to the ladies-in-waiting from the Crystal Pavilion by giving them warm stones so they didn't get cold
  • Jinshi: 8/10
    • He showed his anxiety about Maomao and took the lead not to let her take any dangerous action
  • Lady Lishu: N/A
    • She had an allergy to mackerel
    • She was in a very tough position with the Emperor
  • Lihaku: N/A
  • Ladies-in-waiting of Gyokuyou:
    • Yinghua: 6/10
      • She was passionate and loved her fellow ladies-in-waiting, like Maomao

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 5 twice. When I first watched it, I didn't fully understand what was happening.

I don't understand but somehow matsutake mushrooms were rare and hard to eat. And they ate them just grilled with some salt, and they were so satisfied with them. Are they really that tasty?

Also, for people who lacked knowledge of chemistry or any education, it might've been natural that a fire changing color was a scary thing. That said, I didn't get how they sent secret messages with them. Anyhow, that will be figured out somehow in a future episode, and I don't remember this wooden tablet stuff.

The quack doctor seemed to help Jinshi happily, but he couldn't. This already indicated how high his rank was, and people wanted to get brownie points from him.

The second half was about preparing for a garden party held before the Emperor and getting everyone made up. When Jinshi heard from Maomao that she had been putting on makeup to add freckles because she wanted to avoid danger, he was shocked. He hadn't imagined how poor or ordinary people lived. That meant he had been entirely protected by others, living in a cage of his own — just like the rear palace. He clearly showed his frustration. And I forgot what the hairpin from him meant at the garden party.

When I first watched it, I didn't notice that Maomao mentioned it was going to be a windy day, and she prepared for the cold. So, even though it looked beautiful, I'd wondered why there were so many leaves blowing through the air during the garden party and nobody cared. I was glad the story had already explained it.

Scores

  • Score: 5/10
  • Maomao: 7/10
    • Many people tried to make her eat a lot to get fat healthy
    • As usual. Everyone asked her for a lot of things, and she worked hard.
    • Smart. Figuring out some weird thing from a couple of pieces of information. Doing her usual Maomao thing
  • Jinshi: 7/10
    • Training with a man who was powerful, and showing off his own skill
    • Frustrated by the fact that Maomao had been kidnapped
  • Gyokuyou: 8/10
    • Gorgeous, mysterious robes.
    • She also cared about her ladies-in-waiting and didn't want others to take them away
  • Gaoshun: N/A
  • Quack doctor: 5/10
    • Wanted to get brownie points from Jinshi. Grilled matsutake mushrooms with Maomao, without knowing they hadn't been obtained properly
  • Ladies-in-waiting of Gyokuyou:
    • The passionate lady-in-waiting was good. She had real passion

item.title: Random thoughts after rewatching The Apothecary Diaries Season 1 Episode 4
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I rewatched Apothecary Diaries season 1 episode 4 twice. 8/10. This story was about curing Lady Lihua.

The Emperor asked Maomao to cure Lady Lihua, and he said she was a famous apothecary. But until episode 3, Maomao mostly communicated with only a few people: Lady Gyokuyou, Jinshi, Gaoshun, and the quack doctor. So, he had likely heard about Maomao from both Gyokuyou and Jinshi? That means Jinshi was definitely close to him. When Maomao talked to the Emperor, she was trying not to look at him. When she tested food for poison, she always looked down, or looked to the side instead of looking straight ahead, and she even closed her eyes. So, it's obvious that, culturally, most people weren't allowed to look at the Emperor's face directly.

When I first watched this episode, I thought Lady Lihua's ladies-in-waiting were so ignorant and kept using the poisonous powder on Lihua. It was obvious that they didn't believe that the powder was poisonous and kept using it even though it was illegal. When Jinshi talked about the number of Gyokuyou's ladies-in-waiting and said they were wise, it meant that those in the Crystal Pavilion weren't wise. Apparently, that was true. They didn't treat Maomao well either, even though she had come to the Pavilion on the Emperor's orders. So, they were naturally closed off to outsiders and arrogant.

In this episode, Jinshi helped Maomao in two ways instead of doing nothing. First, he helped Maomao get closer to Lihua. Second, he arranged a steam bath. So even though he said Maomao completed the Emperor's mission on her own, that wasn't quite true. And I found it a little strange that he thought so.

Maomao also took care of Lady Lihua for a few months, and she did many things by herself. She proved again that she was talented and a hard worker.

Scores

  • Score: 8/10
  • Maomao: 9/10
    • Got seriously angry at someone who was doing something wrong
    • Persistent in getting to Lihua, and also took care of Lihua for a few months while doing many jobs by herself
    • Moved other people the way she wanted
  • Jinshi: 7/10
    • Helped Maomao from behind the scenes, or helped a little, when she had trouble
  • Gyokuyou: N/A
  • Lihua: 7/10
    • The voice acting for a sick person was good
  • Emperor: N/A
  • Gaoshun: N/A
  • Ladies-in-waiting of Gyokuyou: N/A
  • Ladies-in-waiting of Lihua
    • ???: 3/10
      • Got the powder illegally and stored it. As Maomao said, she always thought she was right
      • Learned from her mistake. I want to see who she becomes
